Subject: Performance SLO qualification / next steps (latency, throughput, cost levers)

Hi Janelle / Diego —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on SLOs and the levers we'll exercise to get there. I pulled together a short worksheet (attached) that maps your requirements to Redwood options and an initial cost estimate.

Summary of your requirements from the call:
- Target interactive experience: p95 latency <= 400ms, p99 <= 900ms for single-turn generation (user-facing chat).
- Expected steady traffic: ~30 QPS (peak bursts up to ~55 QPS during promotions).
- Concurrency per request: average concurrent tokens ~1.2 (short responses), some multi-turn sessions with larger KV cache reuse.
- Streaming: partial-token streaming is required for the chat UI (low first-byte latency).
- Availability: regional failover between us-west and us-east; tolerance for automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants if capacity constrained.

Primary levers we discussed to meet SLO while controlling cost:
1) Continuous batching / autoscaling profile: configure small batching windows (5–10ms) plus workload-aware autoscaling to keep tail latency low while getting batching benefits during steady QPS.
2) Prefix / KV caching: cache hot prompts, system messages, and reuse KV caches for multi-turn sessions to avoid re-encoding long contexts.
3) Quantization profiles: test int8 quantized profile for your primary model for 2–3% quality delta but ~2x token cost reduction; keep fp16 fallback for high-quality generation paths.
4) Model variants & routing: route 85% traffic to a cost-optimized variant and 15% to the higher-fidelity variant for quality sampling; automatic fallback policy on overload.
5) Streaming optimization: enable early-first-byte streaming and smaller sub-token chunking for the UI to hit perceived latency targets.

Attached: SLO worksheet (breaks down p95/p99 targets vs QPS and expected GPU configs), cost modeling CSV, and our performance profiles PDF.

Proposed next steps:
- You share 1–2 representative prompt sets and a short eval script so we can run a quick quality + latency sweep against the quantized profile (due by 2026-02-24).
- Redwood runs a focused perf sweep and provides a recommended config (batching window, quant profile, model variant split) with an updated cost estimate (deliver by 2026-02-26).
- 30-minute sync next week to review results and agree on a canary plan.

Does that timeline work? If yes, Diego — can you drop the prompt set + a small sample of typical multi-turn sessions into the Drive link?

Thanks —
Marissa

Nice questions — answers below. Short version: p50 first-byte under 50–70ms with the small batching window at 30 QPS on us-west; we'll run the sweep to validate the distribution and report p50/p95/p99. We'll set up an A/B quality harness for the quantized profile.

Answers: 
1) Streaming p50 first-byte expectation: with a 5–10ms batching window + early-first-byte streaming enabled, we typically see p50 first-byte in the ~50–70ms range on a us-west region for short responses (<= 32 tokens). p95/p99 will depend on model size and whether the request touches cold cache; we'll include a heatmap in the sweep results.

2) Quantization A/B: yes — Redwood will:
   - Run an automated metric sweep (BLEU/ROUGE-type heuristics customized to your eval prompts) against fp16 vs int8.
   - Surface delta metrics and sample output diff (we'll highlight potential regressions).
   - Include a small human spot-check (3–5 raters) for edge cases you flag.

3) Peak handling & fallback:
   - If both regions spike to ~55 QPS, our routing policy will first attempt burst capacity in Dedicated pools; if capacity is constrained we automatically route new requests to the cost-optimized variant (with slightly higher latency but lower GPU time).
   - We can configure an aggressive autoscale policy (scale-up target within 60–90s) and an immediate routing fallback which takes effect within seconds for new requests. Existing inflight requests are not interrupted; user-facing errors are unlikely unless both autoscale and fallback limits are exhausted.

Next steps: once Diego uploads the prompt set (thanks!), I'll kick off the perf sweep and aim to deliver the config + cost delta by Thu 2026-02-26. Can we pencast a 30-min review for Fri 2026-02-27?

Best —
Marissa
